The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Kedzierzyn CCS Project was planned as a 910 MWe lignite plant in Opolskie Province, Poland, near the industrial city of Kędzierzyn-Koźle. [FACT] This location is strategically positioned at the confluence of major transport corridors: the Oder River (navigable waterway), the A4 motorway (major highway), and mainline rail connections. [INFERENCE] Large lignite plants in this region typically rely on rail transport for fuel delivery, indicating existing rail infrastructure. [ESTIMATE] The site is approximately 2-3 km from the Oder River, which is a Class IV waterway capable of handling 700+ tonne barge loads. [ESTIMATE] The A4 motorway passes within approximately 5 km, providing heavy road transport capability. The estimated transport access via multiple modes (waterway ~2-3 km, major highway ~5 km, likely rail connection) clearly exceeds the threshold requirement of at least one suitable transport mode, therefore the criterion passes with high confidence.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island (72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint). [UNKNOWN] The site area is not provided in the site data, and no enrichment data is available to determine buildable area. [INFERENCE] As a cancelled 910 MWe lignite project, this was likely planned as a large industrial facility that would typically require 45-135 ha based on capacity scaling (0.05-0.15 ha/MWe for coal plants), suggesting the minimum 14 ha threshold could be met. [FACT] The site is located in Kędzierzyn-Koźle area of Opolskie Province, Poland, a region with significant industrial and chemical infrastructure. However, without specific site area data or detailed land use information, I cannot reliably determine whether the available industrial land meets the 14 ha minimum requirement.

The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The site is located in Kędzierzyn-Koźle, Opolskie Province, Poland, a mid-sized industrial town with approximately 60,000-65,000 inhabitants. [INFERENCE] Given the site coordinates (50.349880°N, 18.226184°E), the plant appears to be positioned on the industrial outskirts of Kędzierzyn-Koźle rather than in the dense urban core. [ESTIMATE] The 5 km radius zone (area ≈ 78.5 km²) would encompass portions of the town plus surrounding rural/industrial areas with much lower density. Estimating the town contributes ~40,000-50,000 people within the 5 km zone, plus rural areas contributing ~5,000-10,000 people, yields a total population of approximately 45,000-60,000 within 5 km. This corresponds to a density of approximately 570-765 persons/km², which is below the 1,000 persons/km² threshold.
